item.title: US Conference of Catholic Bishops says not linked to Trump prayer event
item.description: The United States Conference of Catholic Bishops on Thursday told AFP it was not linked to a group seen in a video praying with President Donald Trump in the Oval Office. “This was not something that the USCCB organized. It is not affiliated with the Conference. I have no further information,” said a spokesperson for the organization, Chieko Noguchi, to AFP. On Thursday an aide to the US president, Margo Martin, shared a video showing the president seated at his desk, flanked by clergy wearing collars. One had his hand on the president’s shoulder and prayed aloud. “Catholic Archbishops and Bishops pray with President Trump in the Oval Office,” captioned Martin in her post on X, including a heart emoji. The White House later confirmed to AFP that the president had met with a dozen Catholic faith leaders, including the archbishops of Denver, Milwaukee and Kansas City. The Trump administration’s relationship with the Catholic Church has been fraught, particularly regarding the policy of deporting migrants. Trump, who enjoyed support from the Christian right during his most recent presidential campaign, has held several prayer gatherings similar to Thursday’s event, including with evangelical pastors. item.title: South-East has better presidential options than Peter Obi – Umahi
item.description: Nigeria’s Minister of Works, David Umahi, has said Peter Obi is not the best presidential candidate the South-East can produce, arguing that the former Anambra State governor failed to consult regional political leaders before pursuing his 2023 presidential ambition. Umahi made the remarks in an interview with Arise News and insisted his stance on Peter Obi’s candidacy was not driven by personal differences with Obi, but by his belief that the Southeast has other qualified political figures capable of seeking the presidency. “Peter Obi is not the best of our finest in South-East,” Umahi said. “He’s not the best; he can never be the best.” The former Ebonyi State governor argued that anyone seeking to represent the political interests of the South-East at the national level should first engage governors and other influential stakeholders in the region to build consensus. “You cannot play politics in South-East without consulting people like us,” he said. Umahi added that if he were seeking the presidency, he would consult widely with political leaders before declaring his ambition, stressing that such a move should not be undertaken without engaging those whose interests the candidate claims to represent. He also challenged the perception that Obi should automatically be considered the South-East’s strongest presidential option because of his performance in the 2023 election. According to him, the region has several qualified politicians who should be considered in future discussions about producing Nigeria’s president. The minister further argued that the presidency should not automatically be allocated to Anambra State whenever the South-East gets an opportunity to produce a president. He noted that Nigeria’s first president, Nnamdi Azikiwe, hailed from the area that now forms Anambra State, adding that Ebonyi, Enugu, Abia and Imo should also be considered. Umahi’s comments came amid growing political discussions ahead of the 2027 presidential election, particularly over support for President Bola Tinubu among political leaders in the South-East. Umahi defended those backing Tinubu, rejecting suggestions that their political choices amounted to a betrayal of the region. He maintained that the South-East could improve its chances of producing a president through negotiations and alliances with other parts of the country rather than treating support for any individual politician as a measure of regional loyalty. item.title: Asian football makes U-turn, endorses Infantino re-election
item.description: The head of Asian football on Friday said the region supported Gianni Infantino’s bid for re-election as FIFA president, weeks after stinging criticism over his aborted World Cup selloff plan. The 56-year-old Swiss was present at a Tokyo meeting of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) when president Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al-Khalifa gave his unequivocal backing, in a significant boost to Infantino’s prospects of extending his reign. The AFC in August had joined European body UEFA and CONCACAF, representing federations in North and Central America and the Caribbean, in condemning Infantino over his plan to open FIFA’s premium competitions such as the World Cup to private investors. Infantino has faced calls to quit and lost the support of some associations in his bid to be re-elected to a fourth and final term. “I think that we reaffirm our full commitment, of course, to supporting you and your leadership as you seek a new mandate as FIFA president,” said Sheikh Salman. “I think you’ve visited a lot of countries in Asia. I’ve spoken to a lot of members within this continent. “I know your feeling and I think your commitment is clear as well. Your support to Gianni is very clear.” Hinting at previous discord, Sheikh Salman told the AFC Extraordinary Congress and Infantino: “Gianni, yes, we had some issues we spoke about in the past. “But let’s not relate the two things together. We need to move forward… football is strongest when we work together.” Infantino, who apologised last week for the failed private investment project, has headed FIFA since 2016 and is running for re-election in March. – Grateful Infantino – In response to the AFC’s backing, Infantino said: “We have seen the transformation that Asian football, and as a consequence world football, has gone through in these years. “It has become truly global. And for this, I thank you very much.” The deadline for candidates to declare for the election is November 18. item.title: FG to complete records of Nigerian casualties, assets lost during ECOMOG wars
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (Rtd), has disclosed that efforts are ongoing to document remaining records, casualties, and historical assets of the Nigerian military and other personnel who paid the ultimate sacrifice in the ECOMOG operations in Liberia and Sierra Leone, noting that it is aimed at ensuring proper preservation for posterity. Musa reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to immortalising the legacy and sacrifices of the Economic Community of West African States Monitoring Group (ECOMOG). The Minister made the disclosure when he received a delegation of ECOMOG Veterans, led by Major General Ohifeme Ejimai (Rtd), at the Ministry of Defence Headquarters in Abuja. A statement by Leah Katung-Babatunde, SA Media, said the delegation paid the courtesy visit to brief the minister on the group’s activities and ongoing initiatives. General Musa acknowledged the significant human and financial resources Nigeria deployed under ECOMOG, emphasising that personnel who paid the supreme price particularly during peacekeeping missions in Liberia and Sierra Leone will never be forgotten. He assured the delegation that ongoing efforts to document remaining records, casualties, and historical assets would be thoroughly completed to ensure proper preservation for posterity. Earlier on his remarks, Major General Ejimai (Rtd) provided an update on the status of surviving Nigerian ECOMOG veterans, noting their readiness to continue contributing to national development and security. He urged the Ministry to address documentation gaps and consider establishing a dedicated remembrance day to honour the hundreds of Nigerian troops who lost their lives to secure peace and stability in West Africa. The Economic Community of West African States Monitoring Group (ECOMOG) was a formal regional peacekeeping and peace enforcement force created by the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) in 1990. Driven significantly by Nigerian leadership and troops, ECOMOG played a decisive role in restoring constitutional order, protecting civilian populations, and stabilising West Africa during complex regional crises. item.title: Rooney calls United squad ‘selfish babies’ after Fernandes criticism
item.description: Manchester United great Wayne Rooney has labelled the current squad “babies” and “selfish” after a humiliating Champions League capitulation and post-match criticism by Bruno Fernandes of manager Michael Carrick. Carrick’s men are 13th in the Premier League ahead of Sunday’s visit by Bournemouth and could drop into the bottom three if results go against them this weekend. With the club beset by infighting and off to their worst domestic league start for decades, Carrick was left clinging to his job after the 4-1 defeat at Como on Wednesday. Deepening the sense of crisis, the captain Fernandes afterwards took aim at his manager’s tactics, saying United had to be more “brave”. Defender Lisandro Martinez last week criticised the club’s board for not investing enough in the transfer market. Rooney, United’s all-time leading goalscorer, said he was in “shock” and “disbelief” at the Como display. A friend and ex-teammate of Carrick, former striker Rooney pointed the finger at the players. “When Martinez came out, I said this is an absolute nightmare because it will rip the dressing room apart,” Rooney told The United Stand podcast on Thursday. “That was the start. We’ve seen it now with Bruno and you’re going to see it with more players because these players, they don’t want to take responsibility. “You can say whether Bruno was right or wrong in what he said but you have to take responsibility on the pitch. You have to take responsibility as a group of players.” He added: “These players, they’re selfish. They don’t care about their team-mates, don’t care about the manager, the staff or the fans, they care about themselves. “If they’re not getting what’s right for them, they’re like babies and just throw their toys out of the pram and go and deflect the blame on to anyone else but themselves.” The post Rooney calls United squad ‘selfish babies’ after Fernandes criticism appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: In today’s Nigerian newspapers review programme, Today in the News, Vanguard leads with the Federal Government saying it has intensified efforts to contain Nigeria’s confirmed case of Ebola Virus Disease; placed high-risk contacts in quarantine, isolated other contacts and strengthened preparedness across states as well as health facilities. Another headline features the National Economic Council (NEC) endorsing a 90-day economic action plan proposed by the Federal Ministry of Finance to consolidate gains from President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms. Vanguard also reports that the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) has warned of possible nationwide action following the failure of talks with the Federal Government over workers’ welfare, petrol prices and other labour demands. Moving to another newspaper, The Guardian leads with the Federal Government saying political campaigns, conferences and other major public gatherings can proceed, pending any change in the public health situation amid the confirmed Ebola Virus Disease case in the country. The Punch reports that former President Olusegun Obasanjo accused President Bola Tinubu of making every Nigerian poor by 300 per cent through the devaluation of the naira, saying the policy has turned Nigeria into “the poverty capital of the world.” Lastly, The Nation reports that former Vice President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has demanded the immediate publication of the preliminary voters’ register, warning that its reported absence from the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) online portal raises concerns about the credibility of the 2027 general election. item.description: By Juliet Umeh The United Kingdom and Nigeria have strengthened their collaboration on artificial intelligence governance and digital transformation, following a series of engagements involving the British Standards Institution, BSI, and Nigerian government agencies. The engagements included an Executive Workshop on AI Governance and Standards, delivered by BSI in partnership with the National Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics, NCAIR, under the UK Government’s Digital Access Programme. The workshop brought together senior government officials, regulators and technology practitioners to examine how internationally recognised standards can support responsible AI adoption, risk management and oversight in Nigeria. item.title: Ministers spend billions to secure appointments, APC spokesman alleges
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Alwan Hassan, a spokesperson for the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, has alleged that some ministers pay billions of naira to secure appointments and subsequently focus on recovering the money. Hassan made the allegation during an interview on Arise News on Thursday, describing ministers as among the most corrupt officials in government and claiming the practice predates the APC administration. “Every time a government goes out, the most criminal elements in government are ministers,” he said. “A lot of ministers pay billions to be appointed, and the first thing they think of is how to recoup that money after being appointed.” “It is the truth about our country and not just APC ministers; it started before the APC,” he said. “The biggest fraudulent people you arrest after every government are ministers.” He also questioned the role of ministers in budget implementation, arguing that the government’s ability to fund approved budgets should be a priority. “Why do we need ministers? Why do we need budget to be given to ministers?” he asked. ‘Power has improved under Tinubu’ Hassan also defended President Bola Tinubu’s performance, saying the administration had taken steps to address challenges in the power sector. He claimed Tinubu had approved more than ₦4tn for electricity meters, arguing that expanding household metering was important to improving electricity supply. “There is no way you fix power issue without having every household powered,” Hassan said. On the use of solar power at the Presidential Villa, Hassan said the government had introduced financing support to help civil servants acquire solar systems. “That is why he [President Tinubu] introduced Credicorp for civil servants to buy their own solar system,” he said. Tinubu will get votes in the north in 2027 Speaking on the 2027 general election, Hassan argued that President Tinubu’s projects in parts of the North would help him win in states such as Bauchi and Kano, where he lost in the 2023 election. “In 2023, Asiwaju was a candidate and not the president. He’s done a lot in places like Kano and done a lot of streets in the North that will translate to votes,” he said. Hassan also cited the renovation of 287 primary schools and more than 4,000 classrooms through the Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC) as examples of the administration’s achievements. item.title: Maradona death trial verdict set for December 22
item.description: The verdict in the trial over the 2020 death of Argentine football legend Diego Maradona will be delivered on December 22, the court announced Thursday, after six months of hearings. The trial of seven healthcare professionals accused of negligence in the star’s death concluded Thursday with brief statements from Maradona’s daughter and some of the defendants. “I hope my father receives the justice he deserves…like anyone else,” said Dalma Maradona, her voice breaking with emotion. The main defendant in the case, Leopoldo Luque, Maradona’s primary doctor, declared: “I am innocent.” Maradona died at age 60 from heart failure coupled with pulmonary edema. The larger-than-life star, who had a history of substance abuse, was found dead in his bed on November 25, 2020. He was at his residence in Tigre, north of Buenos Aires, rented for his convalescence following minor neurosurgery. His death plunged the country into mourning in the midst of the Covid-19 pandemic. – ‘Scapegoat’ – The trial, which began in April, included testimony from more than 70 witnesses. Prosecutors requested prison sentences ranging from four to twelve years for six of the seven defendants, with the heaviest sentence — 12 years — sought for Luque. In closing arguments on Wednesday, Luque’s defense attorneys rejected the prosecution’s argument that Maradona’s death was foreseeable, calling their client a “scapegoat” in the case. Throughout the trial, Luque was by far the most combative defendant, speaking several times when he felt he was being implicated. His legal team played audio recordings, presented scientific articles and even a video of Maradona’s autopsy, provoking the anger of the footballer’s daughters. “It’s easy to attack me because I’m the one who had the most contact with Maradona,” Luque said in court, asserting that “the only one who would defend me would be Diego.” “I cared deeply for him, I loved him, he was my idol and my friend,” he said. The case has revolved around whether the doctors’ decision to allow Maradona to convalesce in a private home, instead of in a hospital, was negligent. The prosecution pointed to the near-total absence of medical equipment, such as a hospital bed, defibrillator or quickly available ambulance as evidence of what they presented as the defendants’ dereliction of duty. Several medical experts testified that Maradona’s caretakers failed to react to key warning signs — he was suffering from edema, tachycardia and had difficulty breathing — in the lead-up to his death. item.title: FG intensifies response to confirmed Ebola case in FCT
item.description: The Federal Government says it has deepened public health response following the confirmation of an Ebola virus disease (EVD) case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on Oct. 20, 2026. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs disclosed this in a statement issued by Mr Oluwafemi Adeniyi, the ministry’s spokesman on Thursday. According to him, such a response to the confirmed case of the disease in the FCT is coming against the backdrop of information provided by the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare. Adeniyi said, “The patient is a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda. “She was subsequently admitted to a private hospital in the FCT, where she received medical care for several days before her diagnosis was confirmed; the patient is currently in isolation and receiving treatment.” He narrated that the government, through the Federal Ministry of Health and the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), is working with the FCT Health Services Secretariat to contain the infection and prevent further transmission. Also, that contact tracing operations had commenced with 44 close contacts identified for monitoring and appropriate public health follow-up. This, according to him, means response teams are working to identify, assess and monitor individuals who may have been exposed to the virus, including healthcare workers, patients, carers and persons linked to the patient’s travel. “Government is also coordinating surveillance, laboratory testing and other essential response activities in line with established public health protocols,” he said. He mentioned that the measures taken by government are intended to facilitate early identification of potential cases, strengthen infection prevention and control, and minimise risks of further transmission. He reiterated the government’s commitment to safeguarding the health and well-being of Nigerians and all residents, urging the public to cooperate with such moves. “Members of the public are urged to remain calm, avoid speculation and misinformation, and adhere strictly to advisories issued by the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the NCDC and relevant health authorities. “The public is encouraged to rely exclusively on verified information from official government channels,” he said. He reaffirmed that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs would liaise with relevant national institutions and other stakeholders, as necessary, in supporting the government’s coordinated response to the public health situation. He further assured that an update would be issued through official channels, as verified information becomes available, while thanking the public and all stakeholders for their cooperation. item.title: U-17 Women’s World ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌​⁠​‍‌​​‌​Cup: Flamingos face North Korea in crucial clash
item.description: Nigeria’s Flamingos face a stern test against defending champions Korea DPR on Friday as they seek to secure a place in the Round of 16 at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Korea DPR, two-time champions since the competition began in New Zealand in 2008, have been impressive, winning their opening two matches to top Group B. The North Koreans have scored 12 goals and conceded only one, underlining their attacking strength as they pursue another title. Nigeria, bronze medallists in 2022, are seeking to keep their campaign alive after losing 2-1 to Poland before recovering with a 2-0 victory over tournament debutants Puerto Rico. The Flamingos will need a disciplined performance against the defending champions, with qualification for the knockout stage still within reach. A win or draw would guarantee Nigeria’s progress, while a defeat would leave their chances dependent on the outcome of the Poland-Puerto Rico match and the applicable tiebreakers. The two teams have met twice at the U-17 Women’s World Cup, with Nigeria winning 3-2 in 2010 before Korea DPR recorded a 3-0 victory in 2016. Coach Akeem Busari and his players will need to remain defensively organised and take their chances against a North Korean side that has dominated its group matches. item.title: One dead, three rescued in Lagos building collapse
item.description: The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) has confirmed one death and the rescue of three adult males following the collapse of a two-storey building under construction in Fadeyi, Lagos. The Permanent Secretary of LASEMA, Dr Olufemi Oke-Osanyintolu, confirmed in a statement made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Friday in Lagos. Oke-Osanyintolu ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌​⁠​‍‍‍‌‌​said the incident occurred in the early hours of Friday at Akinola Street, by Fadeyi Bus Stop, off Ikorodu Road. He said search and rescue operations were ongoing to determine whether more persons were trapped beneath the rubble. He said the agency received a distress call at 12:10 a.m., prompting the immediate activation of its Cobra Response Team from Onipanu Base. According to him, the team arrived at the scene at 12:12 a.m. and discovered that the building under construction had collapsed, with construction workers suspected to be trapped beneath the debris. Oke-Osanyintolu said search and rescue operations commenced immediately, with safety measures put in place to protect victims and emergency responders. He added that groaning sounds were heard beneath the rubble during the operation, indicating possible survivors. He said the agency deployed an excavator to facilitate the search and rescue operation. Oke-Osanyintolu said the rescued victims received immediate pre-hospital care from LASEMA paramedics and the Lagos State Ambulance Service (LASAMBUS) before being transferred to hospital. He listed the responders at the scene as the LASEMA Response Team, Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, LASAMBUS and officers of the Nigeria Police Force from Alagbon Division. He said the cause of the collapse had yet to be determined and would be investigated by relevant regulatory agencies. He commiserated with the family of the deceased and wished the rescued victims a speedy recovery. He also reiterated the government’s commitment to tackling substandard construction and strengthening monitoring and enforcement in collaboration with the Lagos State Building Control Agency to prevent similar incidents. I might be wrong.” Your Negativity, Their Creativity Despite the admiration for their resilience, most members of older generations regard Gen Z with wariness, at best. The 15 Madonna University students, despite the initial public outrage, have nevertheless garnered considerable sympathy over the disciplinary actions taken against them, particularly given that they were all in their fifth and final year at the School of Nursing. Amnesty International has weighed in on the expulsion and suspension of the TikTok dancers, describing the actions as “disproportionate”. The organisation’s published statement reads: “Imposing heavy-handed academic or disciplinary sanctions would terminate the academic progress of the affected students. The students have the rights to freedom of expression, academic freedom and education. The expulsion and suspension are harsh and would create a chilling effect on the enjoyment of these rights.” The organization called on the university to ensure that its disciplinary policies and procedures comply with international human rights standards. Nonconformity, by its very nature, does not always require justification. A quick online poll conducted by Vanguard on the subject asked: “Gen Z is completely rewriting the rules for school, work, and life. If you had to define their ultimate mindset, which trait takes the crown?” Some 33.3 per cent of respondents described them as “unbound or free”, while 28.6 per cent described them as “nonconformist”; another 14.3 per cent said they were “fluid” or “always varying”, while 23.8 per cent described them as “pragmatic” and “system hacks”. A UNICEF-led private-sector partnership study, however, found that despite their resilience, creativity and determination, a worrying combination of geopolitical conflicts, climate and ecological crisis, economic slowdowns and mental health challenges is leaving young people feeling overwhelmed, disconnected and adrift, without adequate mental health support or services. The study, based on a survey of more than 1,000 Gen Z respondents aged 14-25 worldwide, found that, contrary to the beliefs of other generations, Gen Z is deeply engaged with global issues and consumes more news than any other form of content. item.description: Bournemouth pulled off a sensational 3-0 home victory over 10-man AC Milan on Thursday to make it three wins from their opening three games in the Europa League. Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier converted first-half penalties to put Bournemouth firmly in control against AC Milan, one of Europe’s leading clubs. Milan goalkeeper and skipper Mike Maignan was red carded early on for a foul on Tyler Adams and his side never fully recovered. Amine Adli scored a sublime 84th free-kick to make it 3-0, the Premier League side having opened their inaugural Europa League campaign with victory at Real Sociedad followed by a 3-0 home win over Sturm Graz last week. Bournemouth’s Premier League rivals Crystal Palace were held 2-2 by Beskitas in Istanbul, while Scottish giants Celtic suffered a third successive defeat, going down 2-1 to Celta Vigo.
